set.primaryRecommendation: Topical multimodal combination therapy — avoid antibiotic monotherapy
set.treatmentPathway: Step 1: Topical retinoid (adapalene 0.1-0.3%, tretinoin 0.025-0.1%, or tazarotene) — cornerstone of acne therapy. Step 2: Add benzoyl peroxide (BPO) 2.5-10% — antibiotic resistance prevention. Step 3: Fixed-dose combination (retinoid + BPO, or antibiotic + BPO) for convenience and adherence. Step 4: Reassess at 8-12 weeks; escalate if inadequate response.

specificAgents: Adapalene 0.1% gel — first-line retinoid; OTC available; well tolerated
Benzoyl peroxide 2.5-5% — essential for antibiotic resistance prevention
Azelaic acid 15-20% — comedolytic + anti-inflammatory; safe in pregnancy
Salicylic acid 0.5-2% — comedolytic; OTC option for mild comedonal acne
Topical retinoid monotherapy acceptable for pure comedonal acne

set.primaryRecommendation: Combination topical + systemic therapy; antibiotic stewardship is mandatory
set.treatmentPathway: Step 1: Topical retinoid + BPO (continue throughout). Step 2: Add oral antibiotic (doxycycline 100mg daily preferred) — limit to ≤3-6 months; always combine with BPO. Step 3: Add hormonal therapy in females (spironolactone 50-200mg or COC). Step 4: If inadequate response after 3 months of antibiotics: escalate to isotretinoin. Step 5: Intralesional corticosteroids for individual large nodules (rapid response).

specificAgents: Doxycycline 100mg daily — preferred oral antibiotic (AAD 2024 conditional recommendation over azithromycin)
Fixed-dose topical antibiotic + BPO (clindamycin 1% + BPO 5%) — reduces resistance
Adapalene 0.3% + BPO 2.5% (Epiduo Forte) — for moderate-severe papulopustular
Sarecycline 1.5mg/kg/day — narrow-spectrum tetracycline; less GI side effects
antibioticStewardshipNotes: Limit oral antibiotic duration to ≤3-6 months (AAD 2024 strong recommendation)
NEVER use topical antibiotic monotherapy — always combine with BPO
Do not use oral and topical antibiotics simultaneously
Continue BPO throughout antibiotic course to prevent resistance
agentsToAvoid: Oral antibiotic monotherapy — strongly not recommended (AAD 2024)
Azithromycin — less preferred than doxycycline per AAD 2024

set.primaryRecommendation: Oral isotretinoin is strongly recommended for severe acne or treatment-refractory moderate acne
set.treatmentPathway: Step 1: Oral isotretinoin 0.5-1mg/kg/day — standard daily dosing preferred over intermittent (AAD 2024). Step 2: Target cumulative dose 120-150mg/kg for sustained remission. Step 3: Continue topical retinoid + BPO during and after isotretinoin course. Step 4: Intralesional corticosteroids for acute nodule management during initiation. Step 5: Hormonal therapy (females) as adjunct or maintenance after isotretinoin.

isotretinoinNotes: Isotretinoin strongly recommended for severe acne (PGA 4-5), nodulocystic acne, or acne with scarring/psychosocial burden (AAD 2024)
iPLEDGE REMS enrollment required for all patients in the US
Pregnancy prevention mandatory for persons of childbearing potential — 2 forms of contraception or abstinence
Standard isotretinoin or lidose-isotretinoin (Absorica LD) — both conditionally recommended by AAD 2024
Traditional daily dosing conditionally recommended over intermittent/low-dose for severe acne
AAD 2024: No proven increased risk of neuropsychiatric conditions or IBD in population-based studies
specificAgents: Intralesional triamcinolone — bridge therapy for acute nodule flare
Topical retinoid + BPO — continue throughout course
monitoringPlan: Isotretinoin: LFTs and lipids at baseline and monthly (or as clinically indicated)
CBC monitoring not needed in healthy patients (AAD 2024)
Monthly pregnancy test for persons of childbearing potential (iPLEDGE)
Reassess at 1 month, then every 1-2 months during course

urgentFlags: PREGNANCY: Isotretinoin is absolutely contraindicated. Avoid tetracyclines (doxycycline, minocycline). Topical azelaic acid and erythromycin are safest options.
Drug-induced acne suspected — review medications (corticosteroids, lithium, anticonvulsants, anabolic steroids) before initiating acne therapy

hormonalOptions: Spironolactone 50-200mg daily — conditionally recommended; anti-androgen; effective for hormonal acne
Combined oral contraceptive (COC) — FDA-approved for acne; ethinyl estradiol-based
Clascoterone 1% cream — topical anti-androgen; FDA approved for acne ages ≥12
sharedDecisionPoints: Hormonal therapy effective for females with hormonal acne patterns (jawline, chin, perimenstrual flares)
Spironolactone: potassium monitoring only needed with risk factors per AAD 2024

monitoringPlan: Spironolactone: check potassium at baseline if risk factors for hyperkalemia (AAD 2024 — routine monitoring not needed in healthy patients)

agentsToAvoid: Isotretinoin — absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy (Category X)
Doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline — contraindicated in pregnancy
specificAgents: Topical azelaic acid 15-20% — safe in pregnancy
Topical erythromycin + BPO — safe in pregnancy
Topical clindamycin + BPO — generally considered safe in pregnancy

antibioticStewardshipNotes: Prior antibiotic use: {{priorAntibioticMonths}} months — consider antibiotic holiday; escalate to isotretinoin or hormonal therapy
urgentFlags: Extended prior antibiotic use detected — antibiotic resistance risk; prioritize non-antibiotic systemic options

nextSteps: Active scarring: expedite isotretinoin referral — early treatment prevents progressive scarring
Consider dermatology referral for scar treatment (fractional laser, chemical peels, microneedling) after acne control
Reassess at 8-12 weeks; document PGA score at each visit
Counsel on realistic expectations: 6-8 weeks for topical response, 3 months for systemic
Gentle non-comedogenic skincare; avoid abrasive scrubs
sharedDecisionPoints: Antibiotic stewardship: limit duration, always combine with BPO
Isotretinoin: discuss iPLEDGE requirements, side effect profile, and expected remission rates
Psychosocial impact: screen for depression/anxiety; acne significantly affects quality of life
